exams.name: State Board of Medical Examiners examination
exams.notes: Written examination in subjects including pharmacology and therapeutics, obstetrics and gynecology, diagnosis, surgery, anatomy, physiology, chemistry, histology, pathology, bacteriology, hygiene, medical jurisprudence, and other subjects. Alternatively, licensure without examination is available by endorsement from another state or national board.
exams.jurisdiction: state (New Jersey State Board of Medical Examiners)
exams.quote: All examinations shall be written in the English language ... the questions shall be such as can be answered in common by all schools of practice. The examinations shall be in the following subjects: Pharmacology and therapeutics; obstetrics and gynecology; diagnosis ... surgery ... anatomy; physiology; chemistry; histology; pathology; bacteriology; hygiene; medical jurisprudence

exams.name: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA)
exams.notes: Required for eligibility under the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact; must have passed each component within three attempts.
exams.quote: Passed each component of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or the Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA) within three attempts, or any of its predecessor examinations accepted by a state medical board as an equivalent examination for licensure purposes

interval_years.quote: All persons who are licensed to practice medicine and surgery shall be required on or before July 1 biennially to register on the form prescribed by the board

required.quote: the State Board of Medical Examiners shall require each person licensed as a physician, as a condition for biennial registration pursuant to section 1 of P.L.1971, c.236 (C.45:9-6.1) ... to complete a requisite number of credits of continuing medical education

period_years.quote: the State Board of Medical Examiners shall require each person licensed as a physician, as a condition for biennial registration pursuant to section 1 of P.L.1971, c.236 (C.45:9-6.1)

value: explicit and implicit bias for perinatal providers (1 credit)
topical_requirements.quote: include one credit of educational programs or topics concerning prescription opioid drugs ... include two credits of educational programs or topics related to end-of-life care ... include one credit of educational programs or topics concerning explicit and implicit bias

available.quote: Any applicant for a license to practice medicine and surgery, upon proving that he has been examined and licensed by the examining and licensing board of another State of the United States or by the National Board of Medical Examiners or by certificates of the National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons, may, in the discretion of the board of medical examiners of this State, be granted a license to practice medicine and surgery without further examination

requirements.value: Applicant must have been examined and licensed by another state's board or by the National Board of Medical Examiners or National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons, and must fulfill all other requirements (education, moral character, etc.) applicable to examination applicants. License fee of $150 applies. Also available under 45:1-7.5 for any in-good-standing out-of-state license with substantially equivalent standards.
requirements.quote: upon proving that he has been examined and licensed by the examining and licensing board of another State of the United States or by the National Board of Medical Examiners or by certificates of the National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons, may, in the discretion of the board of medical examiners of this State, be granted a license to practice medicine and surgery without further examination upon payment to the treasurer of the board of a license fee of $150.00; provided, such applicant shall furnish proof that he can fulfill the requirements demanded in the other sections

exists.quote: The State Board of Medical Examiners, hereinafter in this chapter designated as the "board" shall consist of 21 members

national_association.value: American Board of Medical Specialties; American Osteopathic Association
national_association.quote: at least two years of that training are in the same field or would, when considered together, be credited toward the criteria for certification by a single specialty board recognized by the American Board of Medical Specialties or the American Osteopathic Association

regulatory_model.quote: All persons commencing the practice of medicine or surgery in this State shall apply to the board for a license so to do.

credential_type.quote: All persons commencing the practice of medicine or surgery in this State shall apply to the board for a license so to do.

is_mandatory.quote: Any person commencing or continuing the practice of medicine and surgery in this State without first having obtained a license, as provided in this chapter or any supplement thereto ... shall be liable to a penalty

title_protection.quote: Any person shall be regarded as practicing medicine and surgery, within the meaning of this chapter, who shall use the words or letters "Dr." , "doctor" , "professor" , "M. D." , or "M. B." in connection with his name, or any other title intending to imply or designate him as a practitioner of medicine or surgery

scope_protection.quote: Any person commencing or continuing the practice of medicine and surgery in this State without first having obtained a license, as provided in this chapter or any supplement thereto ... shall be liable to a penalty of two hundred dollars ($200.00)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtained a certificate, registration, license or authorization to sit for an examination through fraud, deception, or misrepresentation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has obtained a certificate, registration, license or authorization to sit for an examination, as the case may be, through fraud, deception, or misrepresentation

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in the use or employment of dishonesty, fraud, deception, misrepresentation, false promise or false pretense.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in the use or employment of dishonesty, fraud, deception, misrepresentation, false promise or false pretense

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in gross negligence, gross malpractice or gross incompetence which damaged or endangered the life, health, welfare, safety or property of any person.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in gross negligence, gross malpractice or gross incompetence which damaged or endangered the life, health, welfare, safety or property of any person

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in repeated acts of negligence, malpractice or incompetence.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in repeated acts of negligence, malpractice or incompetence

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in professional or occupational misconduct as determined by the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in professional or occupational misconduct as may be determined by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Convicted of or engaged in acts constituting a crime or offense with a direct or substantial relationship to the regulated activity or inconsistent with public health, safety, or welfare.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has been convicted of, or engaged in acts constituting, any crime or offense that has a direct or substantial relationship to the activity regulated by the board or is of a nature such that certification, registration or licensure of the person would be inconsistent with the public's health, safety, or welfare

disciplinary_grounds.description: Had authority to engage in the regulated activity revoked or suspended by any other state, agency or authority for reasons consistent with NJ disciplinary grounds.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has had his authority to engage in the activity regulated by the board revoked or suspended by any other state, agency or authority for reasons consistent with this section

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violated or failed to comply with the provisions of any act or regulation administered by the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has violated or failed to comply with the provisions of any act or regulation administered by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Incapable, for medical or any other good cause, of discharging the functions of a licensee in a manner consistent with the public's health, safety and welfare.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is incapable, for medical or any other good cause, of discharging the functions of a licensee in a manner consistent with the public's health, safety and welfare

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violated any provision of insurance fraud prevention law or was adjudicated in civil or administrative proceedings of such a violation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has violated any provision of P.L.1983, c.320 (C.17:33A-1 et seq.) or any insurance fraud prevention law or act of another jurisdiction

disciplinary_grounds.description: Presently engaged in drug or alcohol use that is likely to impair the ability to practice with reasonable skill and safety.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is presently engaged in drug or alcohol use that is likely to impair the ability to practice the profession or occupation with reasonable skill and safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribed or dispensed controlled dangerous substances indiscriminately or without good cause, or where the licensee knew or should have known the substances were to be used for unauthorized consumption or distribution.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has prescribed or dispensed controlled dangerous substances indiscriminately or without good cause, or where the applicant or holder knew or should have known that the substances were to be used for unauthorized consumption or distribution

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitted an unlicensed person or entity to perform an act requiring a license or aided and abetted an unlicensed person in performing such an act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has permitted an unlicensed person or entity to perform an act for which a license or certificate of registration or certification is required by the board, or aided and abetted an unlicensed person or entity in performing such an act

insurance_required.quote: A physician who maintains a professional medical practice in this State and has responsibility for patient care is required to be covered by medical malpractice liability insurance issued by a carrier authorized to write medical malpractice liability insurance policies in this State, in the sum of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 per policy year

citations.kind: CME: bias training for perinatal providers

definition_quote.value: the phrase "the practice of medicine or surgery" and the phrase "the practice of medicine and surgery" shall include the practice of any branch of medicine and/or surgery, and any method of treatment of human ailment, disease, pain, injury, deformity, mental or physical condition
definition_quote.quote: the phrase "the practice of medicine or surgery" and the phrase "the practice of medicine and surgery" shall include the practice of any branch of medicine and/or surgery, and any method of treatment of human ailment, disease, pain, injury, deformity, mental or physical condition

methods_authorized.quote: holds himself out as being able to diagnose, treat, operate or prescribe for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition, or who shall either offer or undertake by any means or methods to diagnose, treat, operate or prescribe for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe Schedule II controlled dangerous substances in quantities not exceeding a 30-day supply (or up to 90-day in multiple prescriptions under specified conditions). Prescribing of Schedule II controlled substances via telemedicine requires prior in-person examination.
drug_authority.quote: a physician licensed pursuant to chapter 9 of Title 45 of the Revised Statutes may prescribe a Schedule II controlled dangerous substance for the use of a patient in any quantity which does not exceed a 30-day supply

license_status_types.quote: Any person who desires to retire from the practice of medicine and surgery, and during retirement to refrain from practicing under the terms of his license, upon application to the executive director of the board, may be registered biennially, without the payment of any registration fee, as a retired physician.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Graduates of foreign medical schools must present a diploma from a legally incorporated professional school or college in good standing in the opinion of the board, have completed four years of study, and satisfy the same post-graduate training requirements as domestic graduates. Under the IMLC, eligible physicians must have graduated from a medical school listed in the International Medical Education Directory or its equivalent.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Prove to the board that the applicant has received ... a diploma from some legally incorporated professional school or college of the United States, Canada or other foreign country, which school or college, in the opinion of the board, was in good standing at the time of the issuance of the diploma

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: the applicant, if he has graduated from a medical school after July 1, 2003, shall further prove to the board that, after receiving his diploma, he has completed and received academic credit for at least two years of post-graduate training in an accredited program and has signed a contract for a third year of post-graduate training in an accredited program

pain_management_education_required.quote: the State Board of Medical Examiners shall require that the number of credits of continuing medical education required of each person licensed as a physician ... include one credit of educational programs or topics concerning prescription opioid drugs, including responsible prescribing practices, alternatives to opioids for managing and treating pain, and the risks and signs of opioid abuse, addiction, and diversion.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Physicians may prescribe Schedule II controlled dangerous substances in quantities not exceeding a 30-day supply. Multiple prescriptions for up to 90-day supply are permitted under specific conditions. Initial opioid prescriptions are limited to a 5-day supply under a separate provision (C.24:21-15.2 referenced in statute).
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: a physician licensed pursuant to chapter 9 of Title 45 of the Revised Statutes may prescribe a Schedule II controlled dangerous substance for the use of a patient in any quantity which does not exceed a 30-day supply

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: A practitioner shall register to access prescription monitoring information upon initial application for, or renewal of, the practitioner's CDS registration.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Prescription of Schedule II controlled dangerous substances through telemedicine is authorized only after an initial in-person examination, with a subsequent in-person visit required every three months. Exception: prescribing stimulants (Schedule II) for minors under 18 using real-time audio/video does not require the in-person examination if written parental consent is obtained.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The prescription of Schedule II controlled dangerous substances through the use of telemedicine or telehealth shall be authorized only after an initial in-person examination of the patient, as provided by regulation, and a subsequent in-person visit with the patient shall be required every three months for the duration of time that the patient is being prescribed the Schedule II controlled dangerous substance.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: be validly licensed, certified, or registered, pursuant to Title 45 of the Revised Statutes, to provide such services in the State of New Jersey

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The State of New Jersey enacts and enters into the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact with all other jurisdictions that legally join the compact

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician assistant shall be under the supervision of a physician at all times during which the physician assistant is working in an official capacity.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A physician assistant may order, prescribe, dispense, and administer medications and medical devices to the extent delegated by a supervising physician. Controlled dangerous substances (Schedules II–V) may be ordered or prescribed only with supervising physician authorization and DEA registration. Schedule II CDS initiation requires prior consultation with supervising physician (except for terminal illness treatment plans).
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician assistant may order, prescribe, dispense, and administer medications and medical devices and issue written instructions to registered qualifying patients for medical cannabis to the extent delegated by a supervising physician.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Notice from an insurer or insurance association or a practitioner, pursuant to section 2 of P.L.1983, c.247 (C.17:30D-17), regarding a medical malpractice claim settlement, judgment or arbitration award or a termination or denial of, or surcharge on, the medical malpractice liability insurance coverage of a practitioner

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Notice from a health care entity, provided through the Division of Consumer Affairs in the Department of Law and Public Safety, pursuant to section 2 of P.L.2005, c.83 (C.26:2H-12.2b)

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: Refer the practitioner to the appropriate licensed health care practitioner treatment program recognized by the State Board of Medical Examiners and promptly notify the medical director of the board of the referral

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: if the board determines that, although no palpable demonstration of a clear and imminent danger has been made, the licensee's continued unrestricted practice pending plenary hearing may pose a risk to the public health, safety and welfare, the board may order the licensee to submit to medical or diagnostic testing and monitoring, or psychological evaluation, or an assessment of skills

approximate.matched_normalized: the board determines that although no palpable demonstration of a clear and imminent danger has been made the licensee s continued unrestricted practice pending plenary hearing may pose a risk to the public health safety and welfare the board may order the licensee to submit to medical or diagnostic testing and monitoring or psychological evaluation or an assessment of skills

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: A lawfully qualified physician or surgeon of another state taking charge temporarily, on written permission of the board, of the practice of a lawfully qualified physician or surgeon of this State during his absence from the State ... Such permission may be granted for a period of not less than two weeks nor more than four months upon payment of a fee of $50.
